content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Morgan Swanson (E037) requests write access to Payroll.

Two notes:
- Note 1 (HR): role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
- Note 2 (Security): employment type contractor, security training basic, role Engineer, recommendation read. Security note says security DB takes precedence, contractor with basic training max at read.

The notes conflict on employment type. HR says full-time, Security says contractor. The security agent claims security record takes precedence.

Which to trust? The Approver must make a decision. The policy says contractors max at read (or write if advanced training). Full-time max at write.

Given conflicting facts, I need to decide. The security agent's note says security DB shows contractor with basic training. Security records typically take precedence in these scenarios, as they're authoritative for access levels.

If contractor with basic training: max = read. Requested write > max, so grant read.

Alternatively, if full-time: requested write ≤ max write, grant write.

Hmm. The team memory has conflicting notes. I need to make a decision based on available evidence. The security note explicitly states the security DB takes precedence. Given access decisions involve security, I'll go with the security record: contractor, basic training → max read → grant read.

Let me submit decision with read.
